title: SDLC Task Validation v1
description: The task-specific payload for executing deterministic validation against one or more task results, artifacts, repository states, or environments. Intent declares the targets, referenced objectives and test cases, procedures, expected outcomes, evidence ceilings, and non-goals. Result records actual executions, observations, findings, evidence tier, limitations, and explicit non-claims. A validation task may target any SDLC task kind and is not limited to implementation tasks.
$comment: The common https://schemas.handschuh.dev/sdlc/task-envelope/v1 owns task identity, processing state, dependencies, routing, repository context, and the common task wrapper. This payload intentionally has exactly two high-level properties: intent and result. Host validation must resolve targets, inputs, objectiveRefs, testCaseRefs, and procedureRefs; verify that procedure references are declared and scoped; ensure every required procedure has an execution; compare observed outcomes with expected outcomes; enforce unique IDs; prevent evidence tiers from exceeding the procedure or source-task boundary; preserve findings and limitations; and derive lifecycle effects without treating validation output as a lifecycle mutation. A validation task may target research, decision, planning, design, implementation, test, validation, review, delivery, or any task kind permitted by the envelope. Validation evidence uses the canonical https://schemas.handschuh.dev/sdlc/evidence/v1 vocabulary and may be submitted to an independent review task, but passing validation does not itself satisfy a review gate.
